+     You can give the option a comma-separated list of ancestor class names
+     not to document inherited members from.  This is helpful when a class
+     is derived from multiple base classes and you want to exclude members
+     from more than one of them, or when several classes in a module
+     inherit from different classes that should all be ignored.
+
+     For example; If your class ``Foo`` is derived from ``list`` and
+     ``set`` classes and you don't want to document members inherited from
+     either of them, you should specify the option as
+     ``:inherited-members: list, set``.
+
+     .. versionchanged:: 5.0
+        It can take a comma separated list of the ancestor classes not to
+        document inherited members from.
+
